topic: Autolith: A Programming Agent with a Live Runtime

key_points: Autolith is a terminal-based Common Lisp programming agent that works directly in your repository

Core features: filesystem/shell/search tools, oversized-context recursive inference, continuity (portable conversations/memories/agendas/checkpoints/recovery), and a live SBCL Lisp runtime it can inspect/test/extend
Runs on Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD (x86-64 + aarch64); binary release bundles its own SBCL 2.6.6
Provider support: ChatGPT Codex, Grok, Nous Research, Fireworks, Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenCode, Mistral; default model gpt-5.6-sol
Install via curl-into-sh or Nix; ISC licensed; v0.40.1 current
HN discussion (128 points, 61 comments) — author luciusmagn active in thread
Debate over Lisp vs popular languages for agent performance; author argues Lisp's OOB debuggability/introspectability (esp. SBCL) is a major advantage
Author notes LLMs have been solid at Common Lisp since Sonnet 3.5, near-flawless since Opus 4.5
RLM (Recursive Language Model) implementation differs from Prime Agent — top-level agent is traditional but has RLM tools it can call
Self-modification: agent can update without restarting, triage and revert changes, rollback via image generations
278 stars, 21 forks, Common Lisp, created 2026-07-11
README: 'A live, self-modifying Common Lisp terminal agent'
Prompt input is a Lisp REPL — plain prose or exact forms like (describe 'application)
Self.* tools for live self-inspection/modification; lisp.* tools use named heap-isolated SBCL workers
Recursive inference via infer / rlm-map / rlm-complete with shared token/call/depth budget
State/recovery: append-only files, conversation vault, checkpoints, generations, pristine recovery image
Launch HN: Runtime (YC P26) — sandboxed coding agents for teams; a mainstream competitor in the coding-agent space
Contrast: Runtime emphasizes sandboxing/team collaboration vs Autolith's live self-modifying Lisp image
Represents the mainstream 'coding agent' category Autolith differentiates from
Similar Lisp-based agent harness (Jolt) — author of samizdat building something similar in Chez Scheme
HN commenter notes value of canned workflow starter packs for agent harnesses
Part of the emerging 'Lisp agent harness' ecosystem alongside Autolith, sm-harness, kli, pricklypear, fractal-engine

stats.fact: Autolith reached 128 points and 61 comments on Hacker News within days of its 2026-08-20 launch post
GitHub repo has 278 stars and 21 forks as of research date (created 2026-07-11)
Current release is v0.40.1, bundling SBCL 2.6.6
Supports 6 platforms: Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD (x86-64 + aarch64 variants)
Supports 9 model providers: ChatGPT Codex, Grok, Nous Research, Fireworks, Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenCode, Mistral, plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Default model is gpt-5.6-sol; recorded examples used gpt-5.6-terra

angles: Live self-modifying image: Autolith can inspect, modify, and recover its own running Lisp image — a 'Lisp Machine' for agents
Lisp-first control: the prompt is a real REPL, so users can compute prompts, call tools, and script the agent in Common Lisp
Oversized context via recursive inference (rlm-map / rlm-complete) with shared budgets — handles corpora larger than the model window
Robust recovery: checkpoints, generations, conversation vault, and a pristine recovery image make it hard to 'terminally lobotomize'
The Lisp-vs-popular-language debate for agent performance — a genuinely contested topic with strong arguments on both sides
Self-modification as a feature, not a bug: agent can update itself without restarting and triage/revert its own changes
